_note: Single-source (Frankish kingdoms, Merovingian/Carolingian era). Frankish/Old-High-German sub-palette of the Germanic family; the settled feudal heart of the Germanic world. civ = feudal (the crown over comites and duces). Even split Lawful/Neutral. Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Frankish/OHG register (allowed, catalog 5.3); DEITY names are the Frankish-branch reflexes of the common-Germanic theonym ancestors (family_germanic.json), phoneme-morphs of the Agrippan canon, never real Frankish/Germanic gods.

phonology.palette: Frankish/Old High German: the High German shift (th>d, d>t, k>ch/hh); w>w/wu; endings -o/-i; dithematic compounds; theophoric stems are the Frankish reflexes (Dulro-, Erlant-, Giando-, Rialda-).
phonology.phonotactics: CVC and clusters (st, sk, pf, hh, kn); root-initial stress; affricated stops from the shift.

morphology.patronymic_form: patronymic -ing (descendant of); inherited lineage (kunni) for nobility; a Latinate -us form for the higher clergy/officials.

title_ladder.government: feudal (Frankish; the Merovingian/Carolingian crown over comites and duces, the mayor of the palace as narrative flavor)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Frankish feudal, ascending. Baro (free lord) barony; Markigravo (march-count/margrave) march; Gravo (count) county; Herizogo (war-leader/duke) duchy; Furisto (first-man/prince) principality; Kuning (king) kingdom; Keisar (emperor < Caesar) over the Keisarrihhi. (Rank titles are the real Frankish/OHG register, allowed.)

people_name_convention.order: personal + lineage (-ing / kunni); nobility use the dynastic -ing name; clergy take a Latinate -us form.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the secular nobility use Frankish dithematic names; the clergy a Latinate register.
people_name_convention.theophoric: names from the Frankish deity-reflexes + an element: -berht (bright), -ward (guard), -frid (peace): e.g. Dulro-berht, Erlant-ward.

religion._note: Deity-names are the Frankish-branch reflexes of the common-Germanic theonym ancestors (family_germanic.json) - phoneme-morphs of the Agrippan canon, never real Frankish/Germanic gods. Lawful/Neutral henotheist: the One is honored above His ministers; Neutral folk keep the saints and the hallowed ancestral dead at the minster.
religion.the_one: Aiterno (< *Aiternaz < Aeternus; God on high, honored through His ministers)
religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the opposing powers keep their Frankish reflexes + a portfolio epithet (distinct per power; framed as the hell-host): Maraxus -> Marach the War-Fire; Vacidus -> Wachid the Unmaker; Lusanto -> Lusando the Hoard-Worm.
religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Munstar (minster) or Heilagtuom of [power]: 'the Munstar of Dulro'.
religion.saints_pattern: Wih [name] (the holy [name]); the hallowed dead and royal saints venerated at the minster.

holy_symbol_motifs.Dulro: a sun-cross above the scales of judgment
holy_symbol_motifs.Erlant: an iron spear crossed with an oath-ring

banks_patterns.ships: river-trader and saint names: 'the Saint Dulro', 'Swan of the Aha'
banks_patterns.military_units: the [lineage] Leudes / the [count] Lances: 'the Iron Lances of Merovia'
banks_patterns.dungeons_ruins: ruined phalanza-palaces and robber-burgs: 'the broken Burg of [name]', 'the Sunken Munstar'
